items: Passed FCPS Part-I in Medicine and Allied, or official exemption
Two years of the specified training in Paediatrics under an approved supervisor
Certificate of having passed the Intermediate Module Examination in Paediatrics
Certificate of attendance of mandatory workshops
Evidence of publication of one research paper in a CPSP-approved journal

theory.gate: Only those who pass TOACS go on to the remaining clinical components

clinical.examiner: One examiner per station rates the performance and asks questions testing critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

parts: 30 minutes history taking and clinical examination, observed by a pair of examiners
30 minutes case presentation and discussion with the pair of examiners

Interviewing skills: Introduces oneself; listens patiently and is polite
Clinical examination skills: Uses correct clinical methods systematically, with appropriate exposure and re-draping
Case presentation / discussion: Gives logical interpretations of findings and discusses the differential diagnosis
Outlines and justifies the treatment plan, including rehabilitation
Has knowledge of recent advances relevant to the case

clinical.note: Candidates may ask for laboratory investigations; a relevant suggestion earns credit even when the result is not available (p.124)
Answers should be precise, succinct and relevant to the patient under discussion
